This type of insurance provides protection against any loss caused by damage to the structure of the building by fire, flood or storm, plus any loss of contents of value on the premises. Link: “The centre owns a building which has a restaurant and accommodation for fifty guests”.

This type of insurance protects the business against claims by members of the public for injury or loss resulting either from an accident on the business premises or the actions of the business. Link: “It caters for wide range of clients including companies, clubs, students and tourists”
This type of insurance insures the business against claims made by customers relating to the products sold e.g. food Link: “includes three meals a day”

cards.questionText: Analyse how changes to economic variables in the economy have effected businesses like West Shore Adventure Centre.

taskRequirements: Two variables at 8 marks each: Variable 4, Explain 2, Link 2.

detail: This is a sustained growth in the general level of prices based on the Consumer Price Index. Low inflation means: • Spending power is boosted in the local economy • Higher standard of living in the economy • Investment opportunities in the community Business Sales: This refers to a rise in the average level of prices from one period to the next. Sales decrease: When prices go up, sales decrease as consumers will not be able to afford more expensive services. Business Costs: Wage costs: Employers must allow wage increases in order to compensate for inflation and increases in the cost of living. If inflation is low, i.e. price increases are minimal, this has a positive impact on a business’s costs. The cost of running expenses, raw materials etc will not increase dramatically. Inflation is rising in Ireland by soaring energy costs. Business Confidence Low business confidence: Businesses are less likely to invest and expand due to uncertainty over possible economic crashes. Link: “surging costs has highlighted the need to raise prices in order to reach their profit forecasts”.

This is the cost of borrowing. It depends on the demand and supply of money and is measured as a percentage. A low interest rate means that it is cheap for firms to borrow money. • They will expand, creating jobs • Consumers will borrow and spend • Firms are more profitable This boosts the local economy as the cost of credit is lower for consumers and investors. Business Sales: If interest rates are low, this has a positive impact on Irish businesses as sales increase. Business Costs: This refers to the cost of borrowing capital. The interest charged on loans/borrowings from financial institutions. Business Confidence: A decrease in interest rates leads to more consumer borrowing. Consumers will use borrowed finance to pay for houses, cars, furniture etc. COVID-19 Business Loans up to €25,000 usually up to 3 years, were available to sole traders, partnerships and limited companies with fewer than 10 full time employees. There are no repayments for the first 6 months and the equivalent 12 months interest-free subject to certain terms and conditions. Link: “availability of low-cost credit from financial institutions has encouraged them to expand the business”.

The unemployment rate in Ireland is 5.5%. • It is the number of people who are available and seek work unsuccessfully • Low unemployment is good for business as consumers have greater incomes and therefore greater purchasing power. It means more revenue for government and less spending on social welfare. This boosts the local economy. Business Sales When the people/the labour force have less income, consumer spending decreases. This leads to a decrease in sales for Irish businesses. Business Costs: The more unemployed people there are, the more money the government has to pay out to them in social welfare benefits. This forces the government to increase taxes to be able to afford these extra payments. Business Confidence When the labour force have less income, this refers to the percentage of the labour force who are engaged in paid employment. A decrease in employment levels has a negative impact on Irish businesses. A lot of people (employees and self-employed) became unemployed during the pandemic and were in receipt of the Pandemic Unemployment Payment (PUP). As a result a lot of non-essential business activity was stopped for a duration of time while restrictions were in place. Link: “As a result of national restrictions and high unemployment rates, bookings decreased”

Governments use taxation to: • Run the country, e.g. hospitals • Encourage businesses to change behaviour, e.g. carbon tax on fossil fuels Business Sales: Lower tax rates lead to increased sales and profits and boost the local economy as employees have more disposable income Business Costs: Cost of doing business in Ireland increases when tax rates are higher Business Confidence: The tax collected can be redistributed through transfer payments/social welfare payments/pandemic supports. During the pandemic businesses were faced with financial difficulties and the government offered various financial supports to businesses to help them overcome the financial issues associated with the closures. Link: “To survive the business had to avail of government supports during the pandemic”

detail: A meeting is arranged between the employer and employees. The human resources (HR) manager might represent the employer and the shop steward might represent the employees. They discuss the issue and try to resolve the problem.

detail: This includes issues such as persistent lateness, and absenteeism either short-term or long-term. The employer will be expected to have documentary proof of this allegation, such as clocking-in records or documented absences on file that are not medically certified. In addition, your employer will also be expected to show that you were made aware of the problem and that you were warned as to the consequences for your continued employment.

Incompetence refers to your inability to do your job (poor work performance/failure to meet sales targets). In the first place, you need to be made aware of the standards that are expected of you, and these must refer to the job you were hired to do. Secondly, if you fall short of the required standard, this must be clearly explained to you. This should be done through a formal set of procedure. Ultimately, your employer should give you a final warning setting out the likelihood of dismissal.

items.text: Redundancy (due to closure, competition, decline in demand):

Illustrate the implications for a business such as Boyne Valley Farmhouse Cheese when operating in a niche market.

taskRequirements: Three implications using 7 (4 + 3), 7 (4 + 3) and 6 (3 + 3) marks.
guidance: The scheme numbers this response list “(iii)” and prices (ii) “3@7,7,6 (4+3), (3+3)”; the larger allowances are not tied to particular implications.
rubric.markingGuideNote: The official support notes give possible responses, not an exhaustive list. Other relevant answers are considered on their merits. Apply the published allocation to your answer; do not count the same point twice.

detail: If a business decides to sell in a niche market, they won’t make as many potential sales as in a larger market. They may need to adapt the price to increase profit margins on each sale to make enough profits. E.g. Boyne Valley may need to increase their price per item as their sales will be lower

A business may use a niche market to establish itself and build consumer loyalty, before looking to expand in to different market segments, using it’s now established brand-name. E.g. Boyne Valley could build a following in the niche market and then use this to launch a new range

Competition can be stiff in the larger market. However, niche marketers face less competition, as they deal with a highly specific product for a small market segment. E.g. Boyne Valley may not have many competitors as some of the larger firms may not have the flexibility to enter this niche market.

Specialised products involve more costly raw materials, highly skilled staff and job/batch production methods. The costs are high for the business: therefore, they must charge a higher price to customers. E.g. Boyne Valley will be able to charge a higher price successfully as some consumers are willing to pay a higher price for niche products.
Businesses serving a niche market produce limited goods so they may require less investment.
More focused marketing may result in fewer risks and costs for the business, as the marketing is focused on a very small segment of the market.
Businesses in a niche market may not benefit from economies of scale, as they produce goods in similar quantities.
Businesses serving a niche market may become over-dependent on a single product or service and so may be vulnerable as they essentially have “all their eggs in one basket”.

detail: The price needs to be higher than all the firm’s costs on raw materials, labour, marketing, distribution etc. It should also include a satisfactory profit margin on each sale. Boyne Valley will need to add up all projected costs and profit margin per unit at projected sales to set their price.

A price will also often reflect the image of the product e.g. a high price will reflect high quality but could lead to low sales Boyne Valley is selling farmhouse cheese so they could use premium pricing to show that they are superior to other options.

The type of buyers (target market) will determine the price that can be charged to each segment. Their income levels, spending patterns, habits etc. will be researched. Boyne Valley may discriminate between the cheese consumers and the speciality cheese consumers in the price setting process (price discrimination strategy).

taskRequirements: Two reasons at 7 marks each (4 + 3).

detail: Investors such as banks and government agencies will want to examine a business plan before they provide funding. A detailed business plan shows investors that the business has spent time planning and this increases the likelihood of business success.

The firm can use the business plan to set a standard against which it measures, for example, sales and production figures. If the standards are not achieved, action can be taken to remedy the situation, e.g. increase advertising to boost sales figures.
A business plan can help a firm to identify future problems, e.g. lack of finance. The business can then put plans in place to overcome these issues, e.g. obtain a bank overdraft.

A business plan sets out short- and long-term strategies, e.g. one year and five years. It sets out steps that a business will take to achieve its goals, e.g. earn a profit within five years of opening.
